⚠️ **IMPORTANT: new test file is not `dart format` clean**

`dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed test/compaction/structured_escalation_test.dart`
exits 1 on this file — the formatter would rewrap ~15 spots, e.g. line 143:

```dart
return (session, _stateFor(await session.buildContextMessages(), contextWindow: 400000));
```

would become:

```dart
return (
  session,
  _stateFor(await session.buildContextMessages(), contextWindow: 400000),
);
```

AGENTS.md's Quality gates section requires "**dart analyze + dart format clean**". The pre-commit
hook normally self-heals this (reformat + re-stage), but the WIP auto-save commits on this branch
evidently bypassed it. `dart analyze` on the changed files is clean; only formatting lags.

Fix is mechanical:

```bash
dart format test/compaction/structured_escalation_test.dart
```

(CI's fast gate does not re-check formatting, so this will not go red — but the next hook run or
a follow-up commit touching this file will reformat it as noise. Please land it formatted.)

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the escalation's "no foldable range" contract branch has zero test coverage**

`_runCheckpointEscalationPass` documents this as a first-class outcome (gh-2044 semantic 5):

```dart
if (range == null) {
  // Bounded no-op (gh-2044 semantic 5): nothing foldable below the
  // keep-recent boundary — e.g. an entirely pinned/exempt foldable prefix.
  ...
  emit(after: before, ok: false, error: const CompactionException(
    'checkpoint escalation found no foldable range below the keep-recent boundary'));
  return true;
}
```

None of the 22 new tests drive it — `grep "no foldable range" test/compaction/` finds nothing. The
branch is reachable in-run: when the ordinary checkpoint ladder consumes the **entire** foldable
prefix, the covered records drop out of the projection and the escalation's `_pickCheckpointRange`
finds only pinned records → `null` → it emits a user-visible `ok:false` FAILED receipt while the
run verdict stands. Since this receipt also flows to every host (CLI prints
`auto-compact pass N FAILED ... error=...`), it deserves a pinned test.

Suggested fixture (reuses the UT-ESC-8 style): pin the user ask, judge hides one pair, the ladder
checkpoint folds the remaining unpinned pairs so the settle lands thin with only pinned records
projected; assert exactly one `checkpoint-escalation` pass with `ok == false`, error is a
`CompactionException` mentioning the foldable range, no additional checkpoint appended, and
`run()` still `true`.

Two adjacent untested paths worth covering in the same pass:
- `view == null` at the top of the pass (the `hideableRemaining = 0` diagnostic branch);
- the **factory-level** abort wiring: UT-ESC-9 tests the engine's `cancelToken` directly, but the
  production path is the runToken→budgetSource link (`budgetSource.cancel(runToken.cancelReason)`)
  reaching `_runCancelled` through the reason-type heuristic — no IT test exercises a user abort
  mid-escalation through `AutoCompactorFactory.run()`.

comments.author: ai-teammate
ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `judgeCalls` under-reports chunked escalation folds**

```dart
emit(
  after: after,
  ok: true,
  // Marker-only ranges consolidate deterministically (issue #387) —
  // no LLM call happened, and none is reported (gh-2044 semantic 9).
  judgeCalls: visibleMessages == 0 ? 0 : 1,
  ...
);
```

Reporting `0` for the marker-only path makes `judgeCalls` look like a real call count, but a #729
chunked fold makes **N** summarizer calls while the receipt says `1` — the PR's own UT-ESC-11 test
proves `summarizerCalls >= 2` for a single escalation record. This is inherited from
`_runCheckpointPasses` (which also hardcodes `judgeCalls: 1`), so behavior is consistent — but the
new 0/1 distinction makes the inconsistency visible.

Options: document `judgeCalls` as "≥1 LLM call made" on the field, or have `_chunkedFold` count
calls and report the real number (the escalation pass is the natural place to start, since its
whole purpose is observability of a previously invisible deepening).

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-2044 fragile-band escalation is correct, bounded, and well-tested: 22 new tests pass, the full compaction suite stays green (439 passed), `dart analyze` is clean on all changed files, and the boundary table (margin 0 / reserve−1 / reserve / reserve+1), forced-run and `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` gates, failure safety, cancellation, and content-safe observability are all covered. No blocking findings; 3 important and 2 suggestion-level items remain.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ New test file is not `dart format` clean (AGENTS.md quality gate; hook self-heal was bypassed) — one-command fix
- ⚠️ The escalation's documented "no foldable range" contract branch (`range == null` → `ok:false` receipt) has no test
- ⚠️ No curated CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` entry — AGENTS.md: "PRs add lines under `## Unreleased`"; every recent sibling GOAL PR (gh-2003/#2005, gh-1990/#2001, gh-1956/#1961) adds one, and this is a user-facing behavior change
- 💡 `_runCancelled` infers user-abort from `cancelReason is! TimeoutException`; wiring `cancelToken: runToken` at the factory is the robust signal
- 💡 `judgeCalls: 1` under-reports chunked (#729) escalation folds

**Next Steps**:
1. `dart format test/compaction/structured_escalation_test.dart` and add the CHANGELOG line
2. Add the no-foldable-range fixture test (plus view-null and factory-level abort coverage)
3. Optionally wire `cancelToken: runToken` and report real chunk-call counts
